provenance.notes: Out family batch. Young Instagram-first crews; buyers decide on pets, heat, drainage and water bills. Standard direction is C43, not C39 (see whyItFits). No turf or infill brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Pet turf: drainage, odour and dog runs
pageStructurePlus.contains: Fully permeable backing, antimicrobial infill, rinse routines, dog-run layouts along the fence, and what happens when a big dog digs at the edge
pageStructurePlus.why: Dog owners are the biggest turf buyers and their first question is smell. A clear pet page wins them before the visit.

pageStructurePlus.section: Base prep under the synthetic grass
pageStructurePlus.contains: Excavation depth, crushed base, compaction passes, weed barrier, bender-board or concrete edging, seams and nailing, and why cheap installs ripple
pageStructurePlus.why: Two turf quotes look alike until you see what's under them. Showing the base is how a good installer justifies the price.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Backyard putting greens with fringe and cups, chipping zones, playground turf with fall-height padding, and bocce or game lanes
pageStructurePlus.why: Greens and play areas are the add-ons that lift a turf ticket. Buyers come for the lawn and stay for the green.

pageStructurePlus.section: Water bills, rebates and HOA turf rules
pageStructurePlus.contains: Watering restrictions, how to check for a local turf-replacement rebate, before-and-after water bill examples supplied by customers, and HOA approval for front-yard turf
pageStructurePlus.why: Many buyers start because of a water notice or an HOA letter. Answering the paperwork side makes the yes easier.

pageStructurePlus.section: Heat, shade and turf care for families
pageStructurePlus.contains: Surface heat on summer afternoons, cooling with a hose, light-coloured infill, shade sails, brushing the blades, and leaf and debris cleanup
pageStructurePlus.why: Parents worry the turf will be too hot for bare feet. Straight answers here stop the deal from stalling on one fear.

designDirections.name: Ditch the Mower
designDirections.bestFor: New turf crews whose work lives on Instagram and who need one page with a quote form
designDirections.headlineSample: Artificial turf installed in {City}, no more mowing
designDirections.whyItFits: Butter and denim keep it friendly and readable in sun glare, and geometric caps carry a short quote-first page.

designDirections.name: Green Year-Round
designDirections.bestFor: Turf installers with a deep grid of dirt-to-green yards, dog runs and putting greens
designDirections.headlineSample: Synthetic grass and putting greens in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Not the family's brick-and-linen combo, which reads as heritage masonry, while turf crews are young and Instagram-first. The chartreuse accent echoes fresh blades and the grotesque type feels current.

designDirections.name: Backyard Green
designDirections.bestFor: Installers selling custom putting greens, sports courts and full backyard turf packages
designDirections.headlineSample: Custom putting greens built in {City} backyards
designDirections.whyItFits: Basalt and lime on a dark ground makes lit evening greens glow, and the geometric display type has a sports-club feel.

openers.line: Your turf work shows up on Maps with a phone number and nothing to tap through to. A homeowner tired of a brown lawn wants to see a finished yard before they call.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and check for a Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What a turf buyer would land on from that listing: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Instagram bio is the only link
openers.line: Your Instagram bio is doing the job of a whole website. It's great for reels, but someone comparing synthetic grass quotes wants pet turf answers and a form, not a grid.
openers.hook: Check the bio link. If it goes to a DM, a phone number or a link page with no quote form, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Your turf reels, plus the page a buyer needs: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing still has template text in the footer and a gallery of stock lawns. For a turf crew with real dirt-to-green jobs, that undersells you.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for placeholder text, stock pictures or a free-host banner. Note which one.
openers.linkLine: A turf site that shows real installs: {demo-link}

openers.line: On a phone your turf site's before-and-after slider doesn't move, so the best part of the page just sits there. Every turf buyer browses on a phone.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone and note what fails. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your turf site, working properly on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Right now a turf quote starts with a DM and a back-and-forth about square footage. A form that asks yard size, dogs and whether there's a putting green saves you three messages per lead.
openers.hook: Check bio, listing and site for a quote form. If DMs or calls are the only path, use this.
openers.linkLine: A turf quote form that asks size, pets and add-ons: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your dirt-to-green reels are the best sales tool in the turf business. They disappear down the feed in a week instead of sitting on a page that sells for you.
openers.hook: Find two reels you can name by job type: dog run, front yard, putting green. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your turf transformations, kept on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention a yard that drains after the dogs and a green that rolls true. Nobody sees that unless they're already on your listing.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about pets, drainage or a putting green. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those turf reviews beside the yards they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: When the water district sends out the summer watering limits, half of {City} starts pricing artificial turf the same week. That's the week to be easy to find.
openers.hook: Use when local watering restrictions or a drought notice hit the news. Name the notice in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready for the next watering notice: {demo-link}

openers.line: People decide to rip out the lawn on a Sunday evening after another hour of mowing. A turf quote request that works then catches them before Monday's second thoughts.
openers.hook: Call or DM them in the evening. If nothing comes back until the next day, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A turf request form that works on a Sunday night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring turf installers. People who can run a plate compactor and stretch a seam check if a crew looks solid before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring story or note. Note the date and the role.
openers.linkLine: A turf company site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your turf posts tag a handful of towns, but nothing tells someone in {Neighborhood} you install there. 'Artificial turf' plus their town is the search.
openers.hook: Collect the location tags on their posts and use the town furthest from their base.
openers.linkLine: A turf page for each town you install in: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you offer payment plans on turf, say so before the quote. A full backyard with a putting green is a number most families want to see monthly.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing in a post, story or highlight. Otherwise skip.

openers.line: Turf buyers worry about seams lifting and edges curling a year in. A page that shows your insurance and your workmanship warranty answers that before they ask.
openers.hook: Look for any mention of warranty or insurance in highlights or posts. Note what's there; never invent terms.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and turf warranty, stated plainly: {demo-link}

openers.line: A green front yard in August gets the whole street asking who did it. Those neighbours still look the turf crew up before calling.
openers.hook: Look for comments like 'who did your yard' or reviews mentioning a neighbour. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where the next turf referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is a clean turf install, tight seams and a crisp edge. That's the yard a stranger should see first.
openers.hook: Pick their newest finished install and name it: front yard, dog run or putting green, and the town if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That turf job, front and centre: {demo-link}

objections.objection: Instagram brings me all my turf jobs.
objections.handler: "Your reels are great at getting attention. The site is where that attention turns into a quote request with the yard size already filled in, instead of three DMs."
"Then the quote form saves you the most. It filters out the people who wanted a tiny patch and sends you full yards with the details already in."

objections.objection: My buddy can make me a site.
objections.handler: "Go for it. If you want, I'll hand over the turf quote form layout and the base prep page. If it stalls, the offer's still here."
"Some do. The site shows why your base, edging and seams don't ripple a year in. That's what makes your price make sense."
"Shared turf leads go to several crews at once and you pay either way. Your own site sends that homeowner only to you."
"{Build Range}. For you, about {Build Price}: a before-and-after gallery, a quote form, a pet turf page and a few town pages. Less than one dog run."

bullets: Price the gallery by transformation pairs: a turf site sells on dirt-to-green before-and-afters, so count pairs, not pages.
A pet turf page is worth its own line for any crew that does dog runs; it answers the most common objection.
Keep the starter build lean. Young turf crews buy on speed and a quote form, not on a big content plan.
Charge for putting green pages only when the crew actually builds greens; otherwise leave them out.
Peg the build to the base material on one backyard install, never to an hourly rate.
Embedding reels is cheap; curating and captioning them by job type is the work, so price that.

lineItems.item: Before-and-after slider set (per group of pairs)
lineItems.description: Max with grouped sets by job type, captions on base depth and infill, and reel embeds beside each.

lineItems.item: Turf quote form with yard size, pets and add-ons
lineItems.description: Max with picture upload, a measuring helper, putting green and play-area options and HOA status.
Max with dog-run layouts, a cleaning routine and a gallery of pet installs.
Max with green-size options, fringe and chipping zone examples, and an evening gallery.
Max when it covers several water districts' rules and an HOA approval checklist.
Max when each town page gets its own finished yards and local watering notes.
Max when the quote form, pet page and gallery captions are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Dirt-to-green reel and drone shoot
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Film one install from the dug-out yard to the first dog running on fresh turf, ground and drone. That's a season of reels and the hero of the site."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on the next full backyard or putting green.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts of finished turf yards
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each week a finished turf yard goes on your Maps profile with the town, so the listing looks as active as your Instagram."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks after the first rinse
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A few days after install, when the dog has used the new turf and it drained, the owner gets a text asking for a review."

whatElseYouSell.name: Water-notice turf campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When the watering limits are announced, a ready-made turf campaign goes live the same day, aimed at the neighbourhoods with the biggest lawns."
whatElseYouSell.when: Build in spring, switch on with the first watering notice.

whatElseYouSell.name: Yard signs and trailer wrap artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A turf trailer parked on a street for two days is a billboard. Put the name and site on it and on a yard sign for the finished lawn."

whatElseYouSell.name: Neighbour cards after each front-yard turf job
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A green front yard in a brown summer gets noticed. Cards to the houses either side and across the street show the finished turf and your number."

whatElseYouSell.name: Short-form video editing package
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "You film the turf installs, I cut them into weekly reels with captions and the town, and the best ones go on the site."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, if they're already filming but posting irregularly.

withoutAI.route: Turf and infill distributor's installer list
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The warehouse you buy turf rolls from sells to every installer around. Introduce me and I'll build their find-an-installer page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Distributors have budgets and want installers loyal. Their customer list is your prospect list.

withoutAI.whoPays: The groomer or daycare, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The daycare with turf play yards hears 'my dog wrecked the lawn' every week. Their site can send those owners to a turf installer."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Dog businesses talk to your exact buyer daily and need sites too. The referral runs both ways.

withoutAI.whoPays: The pool builder, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Pool builders get asked what goes around the deck. If turf goes in after the pool, the pool builder is your next intro."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Pool jobs finish with a muddy yard, and the pool builder buys websites on bigger budgets.

withoutAI.route: Golf instructors and indoor golf studios
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The golf pro whose students ask about a backyard green needs a lesson-booking site, and you're the green builder they point to."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Golf pros influence green sales and rarely have good booking pages.

withoutAI.route: Daycares and schools needing play-area turf
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The daycare you turfed last summer needs an enrolment page that shows off the new play yard."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: The turf client already has a relationship and a finished project at the site.

withoutAI.route: Realtors staging homes with dead lawns
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Agents with a listing that has a dead lawn call a turf crew before the photos. A vendor page for their sellers puts you on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents refer vendors constantly and pay for pages that make them look organised.

withAI.route: Installer quote helper for the turf distributor
withAI.pitchLine: "Every installer on the distributor's books measures a yard and gets a roll, base and infill list priced from that warehouse."
withAI.whyItWorks: It keeps installers ordering from one warehouse, which matters more than a discount.

withAI.pitchLine: "Dog owners ask about vaccines, prices and play yards at night. An assistant answers from the daycare's own policy sheet and books the trial day."
withAI.whyItWorks: Daycares lose bookings after hours, and the turf client made the introduction.

withAI.route: Lesson-booking assistant for the golf pro
withAI.pitchLine: "Students text to book a putting lesson at all hours. An assistant offers open slots and takes the deposit."
withAI.whyItWorks: Golf pros teach all day and can't answer. The green builder connected you.

withAI.pitchLine: "Front-yard turf requests get checked against the HOA's landscape rules before the board sees them, with notes on what's missing."
withAI.whyItWorks: Turf requests are rising and boards want fewer resubmissions. The manager pays for the time saved.

withAI.route: Listing-photo yard refresh preview for realtors
withAI.pitchLine: "The agent uploads the dead lawn and sees a clearly labelled preview of the yard with turf, to show the seller before calling an installer."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents love a quick seller conversation starter, and the preview ends with a turf referral.

withAI.whoPays: The water district or conservation office
withAI.pitchLine: "Residents describe their yard and the assistant walks them through the turf-replacement rebate form and the photos the district needs."
withAI.whyItWorks: Districts want more completed applications with fewer errors. Your turf client sees the paperwork mistakes every week.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call and DM text-back for turf leads
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When you're on a compactor and miss a call, the caller gets a text asking yard size, whether there are dogs, and a picture of the grass they want gone."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and the reply wording approved.

softwareAI.name: Turf price calculator by square foot and add-ons
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the yard size, pick pet turf or standard and add a putting green, and the homeowner sees a range before the visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their per-square-foot prices by turf grade, demo and base costs, and add-on prices.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for turf jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each new review gets a reply drafted that mentions the dog run or the green, ready to approve between installs."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten of their past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Deposit and completion billing for turf installs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deposit to hold the install date, balance when the last seam is brushed in, sent with a card link so you aren't chasing it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their deposit rule and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Yard-picture turf measurer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner uploads a few yard pictures and the address, and the tool drafts turf square footage and obstacles for you to confirm."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a set of past measured yards to tune against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Install calendar with base delivery and crew days
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Demo day, base delivery, turf roll pickup and install on one calendar per yard, so a late delivery doesn't idle the crew."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their job stages and how they order base and rolls.

softwareAI.name: Turf chatbot on pets, heat and drainage
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'will it smell with two dogs' and 'how hot does it get' at midnight, using only your care sheet and install notes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their pet, heat and care answers written down once. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Yard visualiser with turf and a green
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner uploads a picture of the brown yard and sees a labelled preview with synthetic grass and a putting green placed in it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their turf grades and green shapes and a set of finished yards. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Roll-and-seam cut planner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Draw the yard shape and it plans roll direction, seams and offcuts, so you order fewer feet of turf and waste less."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their roll widths and how they lay out seams today.

softwareAI.name: After-hours turf intake assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Calls and DMs at night get answered: yard size, pets, green or no green, and a visit booked. You get a summary in the morning."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once the form is steady. Needs their calendar and screening questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Turf brushing and infill top-up reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A year after install, customers get a reminder to book a brush, infill top-up and deodorising. That's repeat turf work from yards you already laid."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a list of past installs with dates and their service price.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal with layout approval and install date
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner signs off on the turf grade and layout, sees the HOA status and the install date, and stops messaging for updates."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the install calendar in place.

softwareAI.name: Rebate paperwork packet for turf customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "For customers applying for a local turf rebate, it assembles the before pictures, the invoice and the area figures in the order the district asks."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, only where a rebate exists. Needs the district's form and two past approved applications.

softwareAI.name: Weekly reel caption writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload the install clips and it drafts the turf reel caption, the town tag and a site project note, for you to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their past captions and their approval each week. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing per square foot installed
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which turf jobs really pay once demo, dump fees, base, rolls, infill and crew days are counted, front yards versus dog runs versus greens."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a season of material receipts and crew days.

softwareAI.name: Voice-to-quote for the turf walk
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the yard, say the dimensions, the sprinkler capping and the edging, and it drafts the turf quote for you to send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their quote template and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Crew app with base depth and compaction checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The crew logs dig depth, base, compaction and seam glue with a picture each step, so a rippled-turf complaint has a record."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8, when they run two crews. Needs their install checklist and a lead installer to test it.

softwareAI.name: Sprinkler capping and irrigation conversion add-on flow
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a quote includes capping sprinklers, the form asks which zones stay for the beds and adds the drip conversion to the turf quote."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their capping and drip conversion prices.

softwareAI.name: Commercial and HOA turf bid sheet
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Common-area and parkway turf bids come together from one sheet: area, base spec, insurance certificate and references."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, only for crews going after HOA and commercial work. Needs two past bids.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for turf crew hires
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Turf applicants answer whether they've run a compactor, can lift rolls and have a ride, and you call only the ones who fit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they post for help. Needs their must-haves and pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Turf calculator sold to installers as a subscription
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A turf calculator built for one crew answers the same 'how much for my yard' DM every installer in the state gets daily."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first turf client paid for the logic. Every other crew just needs their own prices loaded.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Certified installer network for a turf manufacturer
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners who like your turf grades need a certified installer near them. A registration and locator portal keeps warranty claims clean."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers want warranty installs done right and have channel budgets. Your turf client is the proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give members a turf site with a pet page, a base-prep page and a quote form, ready to switch on."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewal reasons, and turf crews are young and under-built online.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies picking up turf clients rebuild the same before-and-after page every time. License the finished turf template instead."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell; you supply the trade-specific part already done.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Residents apply for the lawn conversion program, see approved turf installers and track the inspection in one place."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Districts fund conservation programs and need fewer abandoned applications. The turf client knows the process from the installer side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each turf territory gets town pages, a pet turf page and a quote form routed to its owner. Built once, cloned per territory."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Backyard turf packages for new-home builders
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "New-home backyards are bare dirt at closing. A turf and putting green package on the options page sells it before move-in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders like option revenue and organised partners. The turf client becomes the default installer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Playground surfacing request portal for school districts
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The school district or parks department
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Schools and parks request playground turf with fall-height specs. A bid request portal makes it easy to compare installers."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Public buyers need clean bid paperwork, and the turf client knows the spec side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly note on where roll, infill and base prices are heading, built from invoices turf installers share with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Crews re-price often and contributed data keeps it honest.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Dog daycares and kennels, per listing
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A directory of dog-friendly turf installers and pet businesses that cross-refer, paid for by the pet businesses listed."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Pet businesses and turf crews share a customer. A small listing fee from many businesses adds up.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: One turf crew per metro, expanding outward
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A turf installer in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one turf installer per metro, so the calculator and reels stay theirs. {City} is taken, the next metro is open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing territory lets you reuse the whole turf stack.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The turf crew with an unfinished site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A turf site that never got past the template is costing you leads. I can move it onto a turf build already live for another crew."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These owners already decided to buy; they need someone who ships.
